channel.title: Newsnavigator (English)
channel.description: We deliver the news. What you make of it is up to you.

item.title: Democrats win control of US Congress in midterm elections
item.description: According to NPR, Democrats have won both the House and the Senate in the US midterm elections. The Wall Street Journal reports that the party also won a majority of governorships. (Sources: The Straits Times, The Hindu, Fox News, NPR, Hindustan Times)

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race, becoming first Muslim elected to US Senate
item.description: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Senate race over Republican Mike Rogers, according to media projections cited by several outlets, and becomes the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. A Reuters report describes attacks during the campaign, including from President Trump. (Sources: The Straits Times, Al-Monitor, El Tiempo, Dawn, The Hindu)

item.title: Talarico projected to win Texas Senate seat in midterms
item.description: Democrat James Talarico is projected to win a US Senate seat in Texas in the midterm elections, according to Africanews. Hindustan Times reports that Talarico and Gina Hinojosa won their respective races and celebrated at a Whataburger. (Sources: Hindustan Times, Africanews, Mexico News Daily, The Hindu, Axios)

item.title: Democrats win House and Senate in US midterms
item.description: According to DW, Democrats win control of the House and Senate in the US midterm elections. Axios and the Financial Times report internal conflict among Republicans, and Axios says members are questioning whether Speaker Mike Johnson can survive upcoming leadership elections. (Sources: Fox News, Hindustan Times, Deutsche Welle, Axios, Financial Times)

item.title: Trump-backed Senate candidates lose key races
item.description: Trump-backed Republican candidates lost key Senate races in South Carolina, North Carolina, Texas and Michigan, according to Dawn and Daily Maverick. Daily Maverick reports that the results give Democrats control of the Senate. (Sources: Dawn, Daily Maverick, Hindustan Times, The Japan Times)

item.title: After US midterms, several voices expect no quick change in US policy
item.description: According to The Straits Times, a senior Canadian minister says the US midterms will not change Ottawa's stance on trade talks. Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, says, according to Dawn, that those expecting a shift in US policy are mistaken. (Sources: The Straits Times, South China Morning Post, Dawn, France 24, The National)

item.title: South Africa votes in local elections
item.description: Local elections are under way in South Africa on Wednesday, according to several outlets. Voters in Johannesburg raise water, electricity and service concerns, and the BBC reports residents are tired of poor service quality. (Sources: Daily Maverick, The Hindu, AllAfrica, BBC World, Africanews)

item.title: Russia bombards Ukraine's power grid ahead of Abu Dhabi peace talks
item.description: Russia struck Ukraine's energy infrastructure with missiles and drones, according to Reuters, a week before US-brokered talks. Witkoff says the US, Russia and Ukraine will hold talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November. (Sources: Al-Monitor, Euractiv, The Hindu, CGTN)

item.title: All 69 victims of Spanish train crash identified
item.description: Spanish authorities have identified all 69 people killed in a high-speed train collision in Urda, central Spain, on 28 October, according to several outlets. Two Japanese nationals are among the dead, according to The Straits Times and The Japan Times. (Sources: El Tiempo, Politico Europe, El País (English), MercoPress, The Hindu)

item.title: 69 dead in Spanish train crash, twelve of them foreign nationals
item.description: According to Spanish authorities, as reported by The Guardian, 69 people died in the train crash on 28 October, 54 of them Spanish. Twelve foreign nationals are among the dead, four of them from the United States, according to several outlets. (Sources: El País América, BBC World, El Tiempo, Deutsche Welle, The Guardian)

item.title: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta shuts down
item.description: The independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta is closing, its editors say. The Straits Times and The Hindu attribute the closure to state and Kremlin pressure, and Meduza reports that journalists said the paper was to be evicted from its Moscow office the day before. (Sources: The Hindu, Hindustan Times, Meduza, The Straits Times, The Kyiv Independent)

item.title: One dead and six injured in shooting at Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, California
item.description: Police said one person was killed and six injured when a gunman opened fire at a Spirit Halloween store in a mall in Fairfield, California, on Friday evening. According to Dawn, investigators had not yet identified the person responsible. (Sources: ABC News (Australien), El País América, NPR, The Rio Times, El Tiempo)

item.title: Polish president calls crisis meeting after clash at court
item.description: Polish President Karol Nawrocki calls a crisis meeting after unrest at the constitutional court, according to Swedish Radio's Ekot. According to Ekot, the government tried on Friday to remove the court's head, and thousands of demonstrators gathered outside the building. (Sources: Hindustan Times, The Hindu, The Straits Times, Politico Europe, Euractiv)

item.title: Actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86
item.description: Actor Patrick Stewart has died aged 86, according to several outlets, including Reuters and Deutsche Welle. He was known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films. (Sources: Ars Technica, The Hindu, El País América, Aftonbladet Nöjesbladet, Daily Maverick)

item.title: Scottish police investigate Andrew and Epstein's time at Balmoral
item.description: Scottish police are investigating Andrew and Epstein's time at Balmoral. Media reports say the inquiries relate to claims that women were trafficked to the estate. (Sources: The Hindu, NRK, The New York Times)

item.title: Spain train crash leaves at least 69 dead near Toledo
item.description: At least 69 people have died after a high-speed train hit the back of a stationary train near Toledo, Spain, on Wednesday, according to several outlets. Spain has begun three days of mourning, and search and rescue work in the wreckage continues. (Sources: Hindustan Times, Sveriges Radio Ekot, The Straits Times)

item.title: Christine Lagarde to step down as ECB president early, effective 7 February 2027
item.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) announced on Thursday that Christine Lagarde will leave her post as president on 7 February 2027, almost nine months before her term ends in October. According to European Council President Antonio Costa, the successor search has begun. (Sources: El País América, MercoPress, The Wall Street Journal)
